title: Yaw MCP server manifest (yaw-mcp.json)
description: Optional file in an MCP server's git repository that tells `yaw-mcp add --git <url>` how to add it: its namespace, description, entry file, package subdirectory and the env vars it reads. Read from the repo root and, when a subdir is in effect, from <subdir>/yaw-mcp.json, whose fields override the root's key by key. Flags given to `yaw-mcp add` beat the manifest; the manifest beats what yaw-mcp infers from package.json. It can never change what runs: the launch is always `node <entry>` and the build always `<package manager> run build`, so keys like command, args or scripts are refused with a warning. Unknown keys are ignored with a warning. The file is strictly optional -- everything here has an `add` flag -- and a repo may keep it out of a public mirror. JSONC (comments) is permitted.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this JSON Schema, for editor autocomplete.

version.description: Manifest schema version. Current version: 1. A newer value is read for the fields this yaw-mcp knows, with a warning.

namespace.description: The namespace the server's tools are prefixed with. Makes the name argument to `yaw-mcp add` optional.

description.description: What the server is for. Dispatch ranks servers on it.

entry.description: The built entry file, relative to the package directory (e.g. dist/index.js). Default: package.json "bin", then "main". No absolute paths, drive letters or "..".

subdir.description: The package's directory inside the repo (e.g. packages/server). Root manifest only. No absolute paths, drive letters or "..".

env.description: Env vars the server reads, keyed by name. Declarations only: a secret is written to bundles.json as a ${secret:NAME} reference, never as a value.

secret.description: The vault secret name this var is bound to. `yaw-mcp add` offers to store it when the vault lacks it.

required.description: The server needs this var to run.

help.description: Where to get the value (shown next to the secret name).

default.description: A non-secret value written as-is. Ignored next to `secret`.
